IRINGAN, CESO V Regional Director DILG- Cordillera Administrative Region Barangay Center, Upper Session Rd Cor. North Drive Baguio City Dear Dir. Iringan: s. 20L This has reference to your letter dated 12 September 2017 seeking this level's legal opinion relative to the assumption of Mr. Roberto S. Duclan as Punong Barangay (PB) of Maguyepyep, Sallapadan, Abra after being finally declared as the winner by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) in the 28 October 2013 barangay elections. Per representation in the attached letter of Mr. Valentino B. Teneza, Municipal Local Government Operations Officer (MLGOO), Sallapadan, Abra, the following are the facts of the case: Mr. Alfredo B. Bringas won as PB of Maguyepyep, Sallapadan, Abra by one (1) vote over his opponent Mr. Roberto S. Duclan during the barangay elections held on 28 October 2013. The latter then filed an election protest with a request for recount at the 5th Municipal Circuit Trial Court (MCI'C) in Sallapadan, Abra; On 19 January 2015, a judgment was rendered by MCTC Sallapadan dismissing the election protest of Mr. Duclan. The latter appealed to COMELEC; On 19 May 2016, a Resolution was issued by the COMELEC (Second Division) granting the appeal of Mr. Duclan, declaring him as the winner in the October 28, 2013 Barangay Elections and set aside the Decision of Mcrc dated 19 January 2015;

2. With the assumption to office of PB Duclan, the incumbent PB James Fred will slide down to his original position as number I Kagawad. Now, there will be an excess on the number of Kagawads since there was a consecutive filling- up of vacancies. Who among the appointed kagawads will be removed? What is the due process for removal of the excess kagawad? By whom or what office? 3. The excess kagawad still attend sessions, what about his honorarium which is not included in the budget if not removed from office. On your first query, you inquire whether the term of office of PD Roberto S. Duclan is considered one full term. Before we will have a further discussion on this, we shall differentiate term from tenure. Please note that the Supreme Court has a long settled rule on such difference, which was discussed in the following cases: Gaminde vs. COA et.al.: In the law of public officers, there is a settled distinction between term and tenure. [T]he term of an office must be distinguished from the tenure of the incumbent. The term means the time during which the officer may claim to hold ofFce as of right, and fixes the interval after which the several incumbents shall succeed one another. The tenure represents the time during which the incumbent actually holds the office. The term of office is not affected by the hold-over. The tenure may be shorter than the term Tor reasons within or beyond the power of the incumbent. 1 Valle Verde et al. vs. Africa: The word term has acquired a definite meaning in jurisprudence. In several cases, we have defined term as the time during which the officer may claim to hold the office as of right, and fixes the interval after which the several incumbents shall succeed one another. The term Of office is not affected by the holdover. The term is fixed by statute and it does not change simply because the office may have become vacant, nor because the incumbent holds over in office beyond the end of the term due to the fact that a successor has not been elected and has failed to qualify. Term is distinguished from tenure in that an officers tenure represents the term during which the incumbent actually holds office. The tenure may be shorter (or, in case of holdover, longer) than the term for reasons within or beyond the power of the incumbent.2 G. R. No. 140335. December 13, 2000 G.R. No. 151969, September 4, 2009

Applying the above-cited principle in this case, it shows that the term of office of PB Duclan is from 30 November 2013 to 30 November 2016, and it cannot be refuted that the term of office of the elected barangay officials, like PB Duclan has expired last November 2016. However, due to the postponement of Barangay elections, these officials are serving on a holdover capacity only. In other words, they are serving not their term anymore but only part of their tenure. Hence, in view thereof and the fact that the term of office is not affected by the holdover, it is this Department's opinion that the term of office of PB Duclan is considered as one full term and the same had already expired on 30 November 2016. On your second and third queries, it is worthy to note first the long established rule on automatic succession. Section 44 of the LGC provides that: (b) If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the Punong Barangay, the highest ranking Sanggunian Barangay member or, in case Of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking Sanggunian member, shall become the Punong Barangay. (d) The successors as defined herein shall serve only the unexpired terms of their predecessors. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. (a) Permanent vacancies in the Sanggunian where automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (3) The city or municipal Mayor. in the case of Sangguniang Barangay, upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concerned.

This level's interpretation of what transpired in the case is that, when PB Bringas won and became a member of the Sangguniang Bayan on 30 June 2016, a resulting vacancy due to automatic succession occurred on the 7th position of the Sangguniang Barangay. Subsequently, the 7th slot was filled-in immediately. Thereafter, when a member of the Sangguniang Barangay died on 13 March 2017, the rule on automatic succession becomes applicable again. Hence, the 7th member who was appointed to fill-in the vacancy has been elevated to the rank no. 6, resulting to the vacancy again in the 7th position and a new member was appointed to fill-in the vacant position. Later, a COMELEC Resolution dated 19 May 2016 was implemented on 4 September 2017, installing the winner PB Duclan to office. Applying the rules on automatic succession discussed above, it is a rational interpretation also that the first ranking Sanggunian member Who assumed the position Of PB should also slide down to his position as first ranking Sangguniang Barangay member, with the corresponding effect on the rankings of the other Sanggunian members. Moreover, the assumption of the first ranking Sanggunian Member to the PB position shall always be subject to the outcome of the pending case involving the PB position. Henceforth, it follows that the last appointed Sangguniang Barangay member who filled-in the 7th position will be the one who will be removed from the office. In addition, it can be argued that PB James Fred (the first ranking sanggunian who become the PB) already took his oath as PB, thus he will be the one to be replaced by PB Duclan and should vacate the position. However, it should be remembered that he only assumed the position of PB because Of his duty provided by law to succeed and he was not given any other option. To oust him from his position in the Sanggunian is outside the realm of fairness. On the question on whose office will the removal of the excess Sanggunian be lodged, it is this level's position that the removal should be automatic upon re-assumption of the first Sangguniang Barangay member in the office. It is the risk that should be taken by the appointed member of the Sanggunian. Moreover, under the Section 45 of the LGC, it is the Mayor who has the power to appoint the said official. However, as already discussed, since the removal from office is automatic, it follows that no order from the Mayor should be necessary. A mere notice to the 7th ranking Sangguniang Barangay member (who slide down to rank no. 8) of the assumption to office of the first ranking Sanggunian member is sufficient. However, it is the duty of the Mayor to see to it that this provision of law is properly implemented pursuant to his duty over the barangay as provided under Section 32 of the LGC which states:

• • On 13 June 2016, Mr. Bringas filed a Motion for Reconsideration of the 19 May 2015 Resolution of the COMELEC; On 29 June 2017, the COMELEC En Banc issued a Resolution denying the Motion for Reconsideration of Mr. Bringas; However, during the National and Local Elections in May 2016, PB Alfredo B. Bringas filed his certificate of candidacy and won as Sangguniang Bayan Member of Sallapadan, Abra. He assumed office on 30 June 2016; Upon assumption of PB Bringas as SB Member on 30 June 2016, the first ranking Sangguniang Barangay assumed the office of the PB and as a consequence, the 7th position in the SB was declared vacant and eventually filled in; Another SB member died on 13 March 2017 and the vacancy was also declared and filled-in; On II August 2017, the COMELEC issued a Certificate of Finality declaring the COMELEC En Banc Resolution dated 29 June 2017 final and executory; On 4 September 2017, a Writ of F„xecution of the issued by MCTC was implemented. The terminal report of MLGOO Teneza dated 4 September 2016 provides: "PB James Fred, the successor of Alfredo Allan Bringas was ordered to cease and desist further discharging the duties and functions of the Office of the Punong Barangay of Maguyepyep, Sallapadan, Abra and relinquish the same in favour of protestant Roberto S Duclan immediately aher taking his oath ofofifce. " Relative thereto, MLGOO Teneza raised the following issues, and we quote in toto, to wit: l. Is the term of office of the winner, PB Roberto Duclan on this case considered as one full term or not?

Section 32. City and Municipal Supervision over Their Respective Barangays. - The city or municipality, through the city or municipal mayor concerned, shall exercise general supervision over component barangays to ensure that said barangays act within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. Lastly, on the honorarium of the excess Sanggunian Member, it was already explained above that said removal from Office is automatic. Consequently, upon assumption Of Office by the first Sangguniang Barangay member, the 7th rank Sangguniang member who fall-off to 8th rank is not entitled anymore to his honorarium. We hope that we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORI F THE SECRETARY: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary 1 - OUSiÄ; 2018-0 01-01228 L.s/37
